widgets_values:
Edit <Picture 1> by enhancing its existing albedo textures at ultra-high resolution while strictly preserving its original spatial layout, projection topology, and pixel-space arrangement.

The input is a spatially registered texture atlas or collection of surface projections, NOT a conventional illustration, photograph, character composition, or scene. Every visible region represents a specific, independently positioned surface projection. Treat the complete input as an immutable coordinate reference.

SPATIAL AND STRUCTURAL PRESERVATION:

Preserve the exact number of projections, their individual positions, orientations, scale, spacing, shapes, silhouettes, boundaries, and relative arrangements. Every projection must remain in precisely the same location as in <Picture 1>. Maintain exact correspondence between source and output regions. Do not move, rotate, mirror, resize, duplicate, merge, remove, replace, or rearrange any projection.

Do not reinterpret the input as multiple instances of an object. Repeated or similar-looking projections represent distinct, intentionally positioned views or surface regions, even when their contents appear nearly identical. Preserve their individual identities and unique visual differences. Never synthesize additional views or substitute one projection for another.

ALBEDO AND COLOR PRESERVATION:

Preserve the exact original material identities, base colors, pigmentation, color boundaries, patterns, and overall color distribution. Treat all existing colors as illumination-independent diffuse reflectance information.

Maintain completely unlit, evenly exposed surfaces without directional lighting, shadows, ambient occlusion, contact shadows, specular highlights, reflections, rim lighting, or simulated illumination gradients.

TEXTURE ENHANCEMENT:

Significantly increase high-frequency surface detail within the existing projections. Enhance physically plausible intrinsic material characteristics, including microscopic pores, fine grain, textile fibers, weave structure, stitching, natural pigmentation, small scratches, engravings, subtle abrasions, patina, surface irregularities, and authentic material microstructure wherever appropriate.

All enhancements must follow the existing local surface orientation, geometry, patterns, and material boundaries. Preserve smooth surfaces where appropriate. Do not introduce invented objects, new structural features, exaggerated relief, artificial sharpening, excessive noise, or photographic shading.

REGISTERED OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS:

This is a texture refinement operation, not an image reconstruction or composition task. Preserve the source image as an exact spatial template. The original layout, empty regions, background, margins, and projection boundaries must remain unchanged.

For every source coordinate (x, y), the corresponding output coordinate (x, y) must depict the same original surface region, with only its intrinsic fine material detail enhanced. No spatial displacement, content substitution, projection duplication, topology alteration, or compositional changes are permitted.

The final result must be a high-resolution, spatially faithful, shadowless diffuse/albedo texture atlas with improved material microstructure while retaining the original image's exact projection arrangement, coordinate correspondence, color relationships, and unlit appearance.
